focus: A4c v2 replacements for the lost triggers: session.idle, session.compacted, session.created and ctx.client.session.messages across system-completion-sentinel, system-skill-advisor, system-spec-gate and opencode-goal

graphEvents.label: opencode 2.0.32 platform binary (bundle source + string tables)
session.idle and session.compacted are first-class v2 event types with schemas, overturning iteration 6 F4
SessionStatus is idle|retry|busy and session.status is a richer idle signal than v1 session.idle
OpenAPI event silence is an untyped envelope by design; the implementation is the authority for event names
session.execution.started|succeeded|failed|interrupted is emitted and consumed with a terminal classification
Compaction has four events (started/ended/failed/delta) plus the context hook, so session.compacted is not a gap
v2 config key is plugins plural; Config.Info has no plugin key
v2 agent surface is agents plural with mode [subagent,primary,all] and permissions plural
v2 model string regex accepts provider/model#variant, so one model string can serve v2
permission.asked/replied keep v1 names but question events become form.created/replied/cancelled
session.skill.activated and session.instructions.updated give skill advisor a direct signal
session.inbox.delivered, not session.created, gates turn start in the v2 reducer
tui.toast.show and tui.prompt.append payload shapes are defined event schemas

Plugin.Features is {server,tui,rpc} with no hooks flag, so hook attachment failure is unobservable

label: Overturns iteration 6 F4: OpenCode 2.0.32 defines session.idle ({sessionID}) and session.compacted ({sessionID}) as first-class events with Effect schemas, both folded into the registered event union. system-completion-sentinel ports on the same event name and system-skill-advisor keeps an event rather than falling back to a hook.

SessionStatus is a three-way union (idle | retry{attempt,message,action,next} | busy) delivered by a session.status event, so v2 offers two idle signals: the bare session.idle and the richer session.status with status.type==='idle'. A plugin wanting busy/retry awareness must read session.status.

The absence of event names from v2-openapi.json is by design: /api/event carries V2EventEncoded, an untyped {type:string, contentMediaType:application/json} envelope, so names cannot appear in the document. Iteration 6's F5 is true of the document and false of the host; the implementation bundle, not the OpenAPI file, is the authority for plugin event work.

session.execution.started|succeeded|failed|interrupted is a real emitted event family consumed by the host's own event subscriber, mapping to terminal succeeded|failed|interrupted and status running|completed|failed|interrupted. It is a confirmed turn-completion push signal and exposes user-abort (interrupted), which v1's session.idle never carried.

Compaction has a full event lifecycle in v2 - session.compaction.started, .ended, .failed and .delta - handled by a live compaction tracker, in addition to the context hook with SessionRequestKind. Iteration 6's 'compaction is a hook, not an event' is half wrong; system-skill-advisor gains a choice rather than facing a gap.

v2 message reading is an RPC list call - message.list({sessionID, limit:200, cursor, order:'asc'}) -> {data, cursor:{next}} over GET /api/session/{id}/message - not the v1 session.messages tree request. A plugin may alternatively build a cache from session.text.delta {assistantMessageID, delta} and session.tool.success {sessionID,id,content,metadata} without polling.

v2's config key is plugins, plural (an ordered array of string | {package, options}), and Config.Info declares no singular plugin key, so a v1-shaped 'plugin' entry has no home on v2 and is dropped. This is a genuine dual-config divergence rather than a tolerance question.

v2's agent surface is agents (plural) plus default_agent, each Config.Agent carrying model, request, system, description, mode:[subagent,primary,all], hidden, color, steps, disabled and permissions (plural). The v2 side of iteration 5's unknown-frontmatter questions is settled: those keys are real in v2; v1 tolerance remains open.

v2's model selection schema accepts the string form provider/model#variant via /^[^/#]+\/[^#]+(?:#[^#]+)?$/ and decodes it into {providerID, modelID, variant?}, so a single model string can serve v2. The v1 half of the dual-string question is still unprobed.

permission.asked {id,sessionID,permission,patterns,metadata,always,tool} and permission.replied {sessionID,requestID,reply:once|always|reject} keep their v1 names in v2, but question events do not exist: they are form.created/replied/cancelled with client.session.form.reply({sessionID,formID,answer}) and .form.cancel({sessionID,formID,message}). Any question.* branch needs a form.* twin.
session.skill.activated and session.instructions.updated are registered v2 events, giving system-skill-advisor a direct skill-activation signal instead of inferring it from prompt text.

session.inbox.delivered - not session.created - gates turn start in the v2 reducer (started:true only when inboxID matches), so a session.created-triggered plugin may fire before the user prompt exists and must handle an empty prompt. session.inbox.enqueued/cancelled/delivery.changed complete the family.

tui.toast.show is a schema-defined v2 event with {title?, message, variant:info|success|warning|error, duration?}, and tui.prompt.append is {text}. This settles the toast payload shape for sk-vision while the emit path (event emit vs a ctx.tui surface) stays unverified.

SessionV1.TextPartInput carries synthetic and ignored flags, and the prompt builder filters both out before joining text for the provider, so synthetic parts are transcript-only and cannot inject model-visible content. v2 has a session.synthetic event and a POST /api/session/{id}/synthetic route; content injection must still go through context.system on the session hook.

A v2 plugin's declared shape is Plugin.Info {id, source, features:{server,tui,rpc}, state:active|failed} with no hooks flag, so v2 gives no signal that a session.hook/tool.hook registration failed - a silent-failure class that a dual-version template must guard against another way. plugin.check/plugin.list/plugin.add are the sanctioned probe RPCs for settling the loader questions.

direction: Replace session.idle with a derivation over session.execution.* for system-completion-sentinel
reason: session.idle exists natively in 2.0.32 as a schema-defined event, so the derivation is unnecessary; session.execution.* is an optional richer signal (adds interrupted/failed distinction), not a substitute.

direction: Read v2 event names from v2-openapi.json
reason: /api/event's payload schema is V2EventEncoded, an untyped JSON-string envelope, so the document structurally cannot enumerate event names; the implementation bundle is the only authority.

direction: Use synthetic or ignored text parts to inject plugin guidance into the model prompt on v2
reason: The prompt builder filters out text parts flagged synthetic or ignored before joining text for the provider, so such parts never reach the model.

direction: Keep a singular plugin key in opencode.json as the v2 plugin declaration
reason: Config.Info declares plugins (plural) as an array of string | {package, options} and has no plugin field.
